newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends down in farm-related hedging.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends down in farm-related hedging.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended lower on farmer-related hedging and on spillover weakness from other U.S. wheat markets, traders said.
U.S. wheat markets drew pressure from Egypt's news that it bought 200,000 tonnes of Australian wheat, 250,000 tonnes of Argentine wheat and 150,000 tonnes of French wheat.

"We had early buying in the March that helped weaken the (December/March) spread. Locals were selling the spread into stronger hands -- companies like Wilson, Peavey, Benson-Quinn and Country Hedging. So that helped firm up the spread."
Traders said the Dec/March spread traded between 14-1/2 and 15 cents per bushel early but widened and traded at 16-3/4 cents late.
MGE spring wheat closed two to 6-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down six cents at $3.98-3/45.
Traders said Benson-Quinn sold one million Dec bushels early. Atwood-Peavey bought one million March and CIS bought 1.1 million Dec and 600,000 March. Atwood-Peavey bought at least 500,000 March.
MGE barley futures closed four cents per cwt lower, but nearby December did not trade. March lost four cents to close at $6.60.
